report.summary: Reviewed chunk 4 of daedalus/council/session.py: dry_run_plan, _role_for, _is_local_http, default_participants, LiveCouncilRefused, live_egress_seats, convene start. Claims enumerated and checked.
risks: convene line ~1011 | high | Trusted lane downgrade for remote HTTP endpoints may be unreachable if a vendor is in trusted_vendors, because the trusted branch runs first and unconditionally sets lane='trusted' without rechecking endpoint locality; the elif never triggers for those vendors. | Inspect the full convene body in later chunks to see if there is a subsequent check that overrides trusted lane for remote HTTP endpoints.

handoff.purpose: Review dry_run_plan, role rotation, local-host detection, default roster construction, the live-wire gate, and the opening of convene.

symbols.name: dry_run_plan
symbols.note: Returns a plan dict without calling any adapter method; computes seat assignments and bounds.

symbols.name: _role_for
symbols.note: Rotates roles by (index + round_no - 1) modulo pool size.

symbols.name: VENDOR_KEYS
symbols.note: Tuple of vendor keys: anthropic, openai, google, local.

symbols.note: Returns True only if endpoint URL host is in _LOCAL_HOSTS.

symbols.name: convene
symbols.note: Main council runner; chunk covers roster validation and live gate.

claims.text: Exactly what :func:`convene` would do, WITHOUT calling anything. No adapter method that could reach a vendor is touched: only the identity properties (actor, independence class, lane), which are pure.
claims.why: The function reads only a.actor, a.independence_class, a.lane, a.vendor, a.model, a.endpoint; no ask/_dispatch invocation. Evidence methods used are label, digest, paths, files, text_tokens, all pure accessors in this chunk.

claims.text: True only for a loopback HTTP endpoint. ``localhost``-ish and nothing else.
claims.why: Regex captures host and checks membership in _LOCAL_HOSTS (127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost); no other host qualifies.

claims.text: "Local" was a property of an environment variable nobody had ever set; here it is a property of the RESOLVED host, checked, not asserted.
claims.why: The function checks the endpoint string's host, not an environment variable; the claim is about history and design, and the code matches the 'checked' part.

claims.text: Lanes come from the council profiles, NOT from a default argument here: ``codex`` and ``agy`` are ``untrusted`` (allow-list tier ON) unless the operator opts in per council.
claims.why: This chunk does not show council profiles or CodexAdapter/AntigravityAdapter defaults; the lane for those adapters is not set here, so the claim about their default lane cannot be verified from this window.

claims.text: The Ollama host is passed EXPLICITLY and ``OLLAMA_HOST`` is neither read for routing nor written -- normalising a remote Ollama into this process would retroactively falsify ``offload.py``'s ``lane="trusted"`` justification from a code path nobody edited.
claims.why: The function uses the explicit ollama_host argument (or DEFAULT_BENCH_OLLAMA_HOST), never reads OLLAMA_HOST, and passes lane explicitly to OllamaAdapter.

claims.text: LANE DERIVED FROM THE RESOLVED HOST, not from the provider name. ``OllamaAdapter`` defaults to ``lane="trusted"`` whatever host it is given, and "trusted" means the tier-2 allow-list is OFF and ``withheld`` is empty -- correct ONLY while no bytes leave the machine. The bench is another box on the tailnet. Passing the lane explicitly here is what keeps a REMOTE Ollama from inheriting a justification that was written for a local one.
claims.why: The code sets lane="trusted" if _is_local_http(host) else "untrusted", explicitly overriding any default. The claim about OllamaAdapter defaults is from the comment and not verifiable here, but the explicit lane derivation is exactly as stated.

claims.text: Deliberately NOT a ``ValueError``: every other refusal in :func:`convene` is a malformed-roster complaint, and "you were about to spend money" must be catchable on its own.
claims.why: This chunk shows LiveCouncilRefused inherits RuntimeError, not ValueError; but the claim about every other refusal in convene being ValueError depends on the full convene body, not fully visible here.

claims.text: Name every seat that could actually reach a vendor. FAIL-CLOSED.
claims.why: The function returns a tuple of seats; the fail-closed logic is evident: anything not proven safe is counted live.

claims.text: A seat is therefore counted as LIVE unless one of these is demonstrably true: * it is not one of the shipped concrete adapters at all (the base ``CouncilAdapter._dispatch`` raises ``NotImplementedError``, so a class defined elsewhere is the caller's own code and the caller owns it); * its ``_dispatch`` -- the transport seam -- is defined OUTSIDE :mod:`daedalus.council.vendors`, i.e. the test/host replaced it; * its ``runner`` / ``chat`` hook is not one of :data:`_SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS`, i.e. a substitute was injected at construction.
claims.why: The code implements exactly these three checks: shipped_classes exclusion, _dispatch.__module__ != _vendors.__name__, and hook identity against _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS.

claims.text: Everything else -- including an adapter shape this function has never seen -- is assumed able to spend money.
claims.why: If none of the three exclusion conditions triggers, the adapter is appended to live; unknown adapters are only excluded if shipped_classes is non-empty and they are not instances, otherwise they remain live.

claims.text: If :data:`_SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS` ever resolves empty (vendors renamed something), the hook test is SKIPPED rather than trivially satisfied, so the failure lands on the safe side.
claims.why: The code wraps the hook loop in `if _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS:`; if empty, substituted remains False, so the seat is not excluded and is counted live.

claims.text: ``participants`` are :class:`vendors.CouncilAdapter` instances -- read-only, tool-less, spawned outside the repo.
claims.why: This chunk shows convene accepts Sequence[CouncilAdapter] and does not mutate them except lane assignment; the claims about being read-only/tool-less/spawned are properties of the adapter classes, not visible here.

claims.text: Every one of them is REQUESTED, and every requested participant produces exactly one chained turn per round even when it is missing: skipping an unavailable vendor would let a two-vendor council render identically to a four-vendor one.
claims.why: The turn production logic is in later chunks; this window only shows the start of convene.

claims.text: ``trusted_vendors`` is the OPERATOR OPT-IN that lifts a vendor off the untrusted allow-list for this council only. It is recorded per participant, because deciding OpenAI or Google is trusted with this repo's IP is a policy decision and a default argument must not make it.
claims.why: The code sets adapter.lane = 'trusted' for vendors in trusted_vendors, but the per-participant recording and the allow-list mechanics are not fully visible; the claim about recording is partially supported by the lane assignment but the recording data structure is not shown.

claims.text: ``live`` is the SPEND OPT-IN and defaults to False. Any seat that still carries a shipped vendor transport (:func:`live_egress_seats`) raises :class:`LiveCouncilRefused` here -- before the council id, before the store, before the roster is chained, before one byte is dispatched.
claims.why: The code checks `if not live:` and raises LiveCouncilRefused before any council_id, store, or chaining; the live_egress_seats call is the first substantive operation after materialising participants.

claims.text: Offline adapters (fakes, injected runners) are unaffected, so the replay harness never has to ask for permission it does not need.
claims.why: The claim about offline adapters being unaffected is consistent with live_egress_seats' logic, but the replay harness behavior is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Materialised ONCE, before anything inspects it: the live-wire gate below iterates the roster, and a one-shot iterator would arrive here full, be drained by the gate, and reach `sorted()` empty -- a council of nobody, chained as if it were real.
claims.why: The code does `participants = tuple(participants)` immediately at the start, converting any one-shot iterator to a tuple before live_egress_seats iterates it.

claims.text: A refusal that happened after the roster was chained would leave an open council on disk that nobody closed, and a refusal that happened after dispatch would not be one.
claims.why: The claim about chaining and dispatch order is not fully verifiable because the chaining code is in later chunks; however, the live gate is placed before those operations, so the ordering claim is consistent with what is visible.

claims.text: Two seats with one identity: local qwen2.5-coder:7b and BENCH qwen2.5-coder:7b are the same weights on two sockets and would land as one indistinguishable pair of turns. Refuse loudly rather than let the transcript claim two voices it cannot tell apart.
claims.why: The code detects duplicate actor names and raises ValueError with a message about same vendor/model, refusing the council.

claims.text: Explicit, recorded, per-council. Never implied by a default.
claims.why: The code sets lane='trusted' for vendors in trusted_vendors, but the recording of this per-participant is not shown in this chunk; the claim that it is never implied by a default is consistent with the explicit frozenset construction.

claims.text: A trusted lane over an HTTP endpoint on ANOTHER MACHINE turns the tier-2 allow-list off and reports ``withheld=[]`` while full repo source crosses the tailnet. That is precisely the justification ``offload.py:193-197`` rests on ("no bytes leave the machine"), borrowed by a host it was never written for. Fail closed and make
claims.why: The comment is cut off and the actual downgrade logic is not fully shown; the code in this chunk only starts the elif branch, so the full behavior cannot be verified.

observations.what: In convene, the trusted_vendors branch sets adapter.lane = 'trusted' unconditionally for any vendor in trusted_vendors, even if the endpoint is a remote HTTP host. The subsequent elif that downgrades trusted lanes on remote HTTP endpoints will never fire for those vendors, because the first branch already set the lane to 'trusted' and the elif condition checks lane == 'trusted' but the branch is elif, so it is skipped.

The dry_run_plan function uses _role_for with index i and round r, but the role assignment may differ from convene's actual role assignment, which is not visible in this chunk; this could make the dry run plan inconsistent with the real run.

The live_egress_seats function checks _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS for hook identity, but the variable is not defined in this chunk; it is a module-level constant from earlier in the file. The claim that it is defined is uncheckable, but the logic depends on it.

The comment in convene about 'open council on disk' implies that convene writes a council store, but the store path is computed later in this chunk (store = Path(store_path) ...), and the actual store opening is not shown. The live gate runs before the store is created, consistent with the comment.
The default_participants function imports vendor adapters inside the function, which is a deliberate lazy import to avoid circular imports; this is not a defect but a design choice.
